correctness.rationale: Newton identities and symmetric-polynomial freeness yield a regular sequence in all allowed cases. Exact Vandermonde rank and invertibility of nonzero coordinate multiplicities prove smoothness for n<p; p equal nonzero coordinates witness singularity for n>=p. Binomial translation at n=p is an exact triangular equality of ideals. The smooth base and homogeneous complete intersection prove unique vertex and local multiplicity m!, with connectedness, CM and Serre criteria distinguishing the three boundary regimes. The finite checker does not replace these arguments.

value.rationale: Exact smoothness and singularity thresholds directly address the motivating paper’s geometrical question. The natural first singular member has a computable scheme-theoretic local multiplicity and changes from a fat point to a line arrangement to a normal cone in sharp arithmetic regimes. This supplies useful boundary geometry not entailed by generic CI/normality bounds, with a stated limited family.
